\isamarkupsection{Alphabet reduction: reverse language inclusion%
}
\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
The reverse leg of \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}language}:
  \isa{encode{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}input{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}ar\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}{\isasymGamma}{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}bl{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}\ w\ {\isasymin}\ Lang{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}\ {\isasymLongrightarrow}\ w\ {\isasymin}\ Lang{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm\ M}, the converse of the proven
  \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}language{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}forward}.

  Unlike AE's reverse arm, which restricts to \isa{det{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm\ M} and
  closes via chain uniqueness (Path C), AR proves this
  unconditionally — deterministic and nondeterministic \isa{M}
  alike.  The counterexample probe is negative: AR's
  nondeterminism gateway \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}compute} is a direct
  single-step embedding of \isa{delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M} (one substrate tuple per
  \isa{M}-tuple, no AE-style \isa{m{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}steps{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}buffered} slack), so every
  accepting \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-path decodes branch-by-branch to a genuine
  accepting \isa{M}-path.

  Strategy (Strategy B, direct backward inversion): a per-cycle
  backward step lemma reads the \isa{M}-transition straight off the
  compute tuple on the given \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-path and reuses the forward
  arm's invariants \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}simulates}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}posk{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}consistent},
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}boundary} read backward; a backward chunked engine
  aggregates the per-cycle steps into an \isa{M}-run.
  Throughout, \isa{b} abbreviates \isa{block{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}width\ {\isasymGamma}} (the per-symbol cell width).%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Base case of the backward engine: the accept state
  \isa{t{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}} is terminal.  A valid machine never
  steps from its accept state (substrate \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}neq{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}t}),
  and \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce\ M} is valid by \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}wf};
  its accept state is \isa{{\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}t{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}accept{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}stage\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}bl{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}} by
  \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}accept}.

  Itself currently uncalled: the backward engine kills reject boundaries
  mid-trace via \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reject{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}terminal}, not accept ones; retained as the
  documented half of the accept/reject terminal pair.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Reject companion of \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}accept{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}terminal}: the reject state
  \isa{r{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}r{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reject{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}stage\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}bl{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}
  (by \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reject}) is terminal too (substrate
  \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}neq{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}r}).  The backward engine uses it to kill a
  reject boundary reached mid-trace: the trace runs to the accept
  config, so a reject config can carry no outgoing step.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Each of the five substep relations carries a uniform source
  substep-tag (\isa{fst\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}snd\ s{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}} for a source state \isa{s\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}q{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ stg{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}),
  and the five tags are pairwise distinct datatype constructors.  This
  is the structural fact every step-inversion lemma rests on: a step
  whose source is at substep \isa{X} can only come from the relation
  whose sources carry tag \isa{X}.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Each substep relation's destination tag is confined to a
  small set: read loops to itself or transitions to compute; compute
  is the unique non-deterministic step and lands at write; write
  loops or advances; advance loops or hands off to next; next closes
  the cycle (back to read) or dispatches to a halt-coerced
  configuration.  These five facts encode the substep transition
  graph and underpin the chain-shape arguments used in the reverse
  arm's pinning lemmas.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
The keystone of the reverse arm: a single \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-step out of
  an \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimCompute} configuration reads the simulated
  \isa{M}-transition straight off the compute tuple.  Because
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}compute} is a direct single-step embedding of
  \isa{delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M}, the inversion yields a genuine
  \isa{{\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}q{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ buf{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ q{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ m{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}a{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ m{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}d{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}\ {\isasymin}\ delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M} with no chain-uniqueness
  or determinism assumption — this is where AR's ND-generality is
  earned.  Compute neither writes nor moves: the tape and head
  positions are unchanged (read symbol equals write symbol, direction
  \isa{N}).%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
A single \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-step out of an \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimNext}
  configuration neither writes nor moves, and dispatches on the
  simulated \isa{M}-state \isa{q}: continue to the next
  \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimRead} boundary when \isa{q} is non-halting, or land
  in the accept/reject halt stage when \isa{q} is \isa{M}'s
  accept/reject state.  The accept landing is exactly
  \isa{t{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
The read relation is a *function* of (source state, read
  symbol): for a fixed source \isa{s} and read vector \isa{a} the
  target state, written vector, and direction are uniquely determined.
  The seven arms partition by the bit-counter \isa{i}, then within an
  \isa{i}-class by \isa{posk\ tk} / \isa{a\ tk} / \isa{is{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}last{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}k\ M\ tk}.
  The one non-obvious exclusion is arm 4 (\isa{i\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ Suc\ {\isadigit{0}}}) versus arms
  6/7 (\isa{i\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ Suc\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}b{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}): these collide only if
  \isa{b\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ {\isadigit{0}}}, ruled out by \isa{block{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}width{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}pos} (which is
  therefore load-bearing here, not decorative).%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Write is a function of (source, read vector): the LE arms
  (\isa{buf\ tk\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ le}) split from the proper arms by the buf cell,
  and the proper back-walk / forward-write / boundary arms partition by
  the bit-counter ranges \isa{{\isacharbrackleft}{\kern0pt}{\isadigit{0}}{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ b{\isacharminus}{\kern0pt}{\isadigit{1}}{\isacharbrackright}{\kern0pt}}, \isa{{\isacharbrackleft}{\kern0pt}b{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ {\isadigit{2}}b{\isacharminus}{\kern0pt}{\isadigit{2}}{\isacharbrackright}{\kern0pt}},
  \isa{{\isacharbraceleft}{\kern0pt}{\isadigit{2}}b{\isacharminus}{\kern0pt}{\isadigit{1}}{\isacharbraceright}{\kern0pt}}, separated arithmetically; \isa{is{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}last{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}k} splits
  the last-tape arms.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Lift the per-relation destination-tag lemmas
  (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}X{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}dest}) up through \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}: an
  \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-step out of a configuration whose source idx is
  \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimX} lands at a configuration whose idx is in
  \isa{X}'s dest set.  The five lemmas compose
  \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isachardot}{\kern0pt}cases} (extract the firing tuple), the
  \isa{from{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src} union-disambiguation helpers, and
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}X{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}dest}.  Together they encode the cycle's
  substep transition graph at the level the substep-walker engine
  consumes: SimRead-loop-or-compute, compute-to-write,
  write-loop-or-advance, advance-loop-or-next,
  next-to-read-or-halt.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\isamarkupsubsection{Walker invariants — per-substep stage predicates%
}
\isamarkuptrue%
%
\endisatagdocument
{\isafolddocument}%

\isadelimdocument

%
\begin{isamarkuptext}%
The substep-walker is a per-step induction over the
\isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-path that tracks where in the cycle we are by reading
the substep idx off each visited configuration's state.  Six stage
predicates carry the per-substep relationship between the cycle's
source \isa{M}-config \isa{cM} and the current
\isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-configuration \isa{c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}:

%
\begin{itemize}%
\item \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}boundary\ M\ cM\ c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}: fresh cycle start —
\isa{c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}} at \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimRead} boundary, the three
forward invariants hold for \isa{cM}.

\item \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read\ M\ cM\ c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}: mid-read-phase —
reachable from a boundary by \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read}-only
steps, still at \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimRead}.

\item \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}compute\ M\ cM\ c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}: read complete —
reachable from a boundary by \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read}-only
steps, now at \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimCompute}.  The next M'-step on
the path extracts the M-tuple via
\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}compute{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}inv}.

\item \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write\ M\ cM\ c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}: M-tuple
extracted, mid-write-phase — at \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimWrite}.

\item \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance\ M\ cM\ c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}: write done,
mid-advance-phase — at \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimAdvance}.

\item \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}next\ M\ cM\ c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}: at
\isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimNext}, about to dispatch to next boundary or
halt via \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}next{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}inv}.

The witness-chain formulation (rather than concrete per-state
conditions) makes preservation lemmas mechanical: at a config with
substep tag T, an M'-step fires the unique substep relation with
src tag T (by \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}T{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src} + \isa{from{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src});
extending the witness chain by one step preserves the invariant.
Chain shape (no cycle-wrap before completing this cycle) follows
from the witness chain living in the *specific* substep relation
\isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}T\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}, which by
\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}T{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src} can only fire from sources at T —
ruling out the wrap.%
\end{itemize}%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Five \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}-to-specific-substep lifts: an
  \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-step in \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}
  whose source carries substep tag T is in fact in the smaller
  \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}T\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}.  Each composes
  \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isachardot}{\kern0pt}cases} (destructure the step), the matching
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}T{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}from{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src} helper (narrow the firing tuple by
  src-tag uniqueness), and \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isachardot}{\kern0pt}step} with
  \isa{where\ ts\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ ts\ and\ n\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ n} instantiation (break the
  higher-order unification ambiguity inherent in
  \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isachardot}{\kern0pt}step}'s pattern when matched against concrete
  tuples).  The walker preservation lemmas chain these lifts with
  the dest-tag dispatch (lands-at lemmas) to advance the witness
  chain by one step.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\isamarkupsubsection{Chain pinning in \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Two structural facts about chains in the read sub-relation:
  the sub-relation is *functional* (lifted from
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}func} via \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}'s shape), so its
  \isa{m}-step extension of any seed is unique; and it cannot fire
  from a source whose substep tag is \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimCompute} (by
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src}).  Together these pin a chain ending at
  \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimCompute} uniquely on both its length and its endpoint:
  if two chains in the sub-relation start at the same seed and both
  end at an \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimCompute}-tagged config, they coincide.  This
  is what bridges the walker's by-construction \isa{R{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read} witness
  chain to the existence chain produced by the (re-mirrored)
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}phase{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}sub}: the witness chain inherits the latter's
  stated endpoint state shape, including the load-bearing
  \isa{buf\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ {\isasymlambda}k{\isachardot}{\kern0pt}\ mt{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tape\ cM\ k\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}mt{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}pos\ cM\ k{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Two parallel chain-pinning suites for the write and advance
  sub-relations, mirroring the read suite verbatim with
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write} / \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance} in place of
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read} and \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimAdvance} / \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimNext}
  in place of \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimCompute}.  Functional projections
  (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}func}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}func}) and src
  uniqueness (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}src})
  feed the same scaffold.  These suites are used by the cycle-close
  bridging lemma to pin walker write/advance chains against the
  forward \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}phase} / \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}phase}
  constructions.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
For each single-step read-phase leaf
  (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}le{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}le{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}finish{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step},
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}lookback{\isadigit{1}}{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}lookback{\isadigit{2}}{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step},
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}bit{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}bit{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}boundary{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step},
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}bit{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}finish{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}), a companion lemma producing the
  step in \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}} instead of
  \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}.  Each variant uses the
  existing lemma to obtain the step, then lifts via
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}lift} (the source tag is \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimRead} by
  the leaf's \isa{stg} hypothesis).  No re-derivation of the step's
  effect — the existing leaf's stated post-state, post-tape, post-pos
  conclusions flow through verbatim.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Multi-step combiner \isa{{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}sub} variants follow the same
  proof structure as the originals, but obtain their sub-chains from
  the leaf \isa{{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}sub} companions and compose via the generic
  \isa{relpow{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}Suc{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}I{\isadigit{2}}}/\isa{relpow{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}add} combinators (which work over
  any relation, in particular \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}}).
  All bookkeeping for tape, position, state shape transfers verbatim
  from the originals.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Three advance-phase leaves
  (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walk{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}boundary{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step},
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}finish{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step}) mirror to the sub-relation
  \isa{mttm{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}} via
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}exists{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}sub{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance}, parallel to the write and
  read leaves above.  Each variant derives the
  \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimAdvance} source tag from \isa{stg}, then composes
  the original leaf with the existence lifter.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
One preservation lemma per substep predicate: an
  \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-step out of a config satisfying the current invariant
  lands at a config satisfying the next invariant in the cycle (or
  splits the disjunction when the substep's relation has multiple
  destination arms).  Together with the chunked engine, these
  characterise the walker's per-step evolution: the substep idx
  carried in the M'-config is the dispatch discriminator at each
  step, no chain pinning needed.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
The sixth and final substep preservation closes the
  walker suite mechanically: an \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-step out of
  \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimNext} lands at \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimRead} (cycle close),
  \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}HaltAccept}, or \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}HaltReject} by
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}from{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimNext{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}lands}.  This is a pure dispatch
  lemma — establishing the boundary for the reconstructed
  \isa{M}-successor at a cycle close is a separate cycle-level
  concern handled by \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}cycle{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}close} and the chunked
  reverse engine.  Keeping the \isa{at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}next} walker preservation
  thin keeps the suite uniform — all six are one-substep
  mechanical lemmas.  Itself currently uncalled — the cycle close runs
  through \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}cycle{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}close} directly — kept to complete the
  six-member walker-preservation suite.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
An \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimNext} step closes a simulation cycle: the walker is
  re-established at a boundary for the next \isa{M}-configuration.  The
  successor is \emph{reconstructed} from the pinned compute branch
  (the \isa{{\isasymexists}cM{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}} in the conclusion): under nondeterministic
  \isa{delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M} the source \isa{cM} may have several successors, so the
  fired branch is recovered from the walker's own witness chain rather
  than assumed.  The forward
  arm is rebuilt entirely over the substep sub-relations and each walker
  witness chain is pinned by a \isa{chain{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}delta{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}X{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}to{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}Y{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}uniq} suite.

  The closing next step is inverted by \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}next{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}inv}, which
  dispatches on the reconstructed \isa{M}-state \isa{q{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}} into three
  outcomes: continue (\isa{q{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}\ {\isasymnotin}\ {\isacharbraceleft}{\kern0pt}t{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ r{\isacharbraceright}{\kern0pt}}, landing at \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimRead}),
  accept (\isa{q{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ t{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M}) or reject (\isa{q{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ r{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M}).  All three
  re-establish \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}boundary\ M\ cMn\ c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}: the boundary
  invariant carries the halt cases too — \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}simulates}'s state
  disjunction has dedicated accept/reject arms, and both
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}posk{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}consistent} and \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}boundary} are
  \isa{AR{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}SimRead}-guarded, hence vacuous off the read boundary.  The
  three predicates are discharged from the explicit endpoint by the shared
  semantic lemmas (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tape{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}correspondence},
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}newsimpos}, \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}newpos{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}atLE{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}iff}).  No union chain
  is pinned and \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}simulates{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}forward{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}step} is not invoked.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
The reverse-arm loop invariant: the substep-walker is in
  \emph{some} stage of the cycle.  Six disjuncts, one per walker
  predicate.  This is the AR analogue of
  carrying \isa{ae{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}simulates} across AE's reverse induction, but
  stage-granular: where AE peels a whole fixed-length cycle per
  \isa{ae{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}backward{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}stage}, AR peels one \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-substep and dispatches on
  the current substep tag (the cycle length is data-dependent here, which
  is why the pivot to the substep walker was needed in the first place).%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Chunked-induction engine for the reverse arm, the AR analogue of
AE's \isa{ae{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}simulation{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}phase{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}chunked{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reverse}.  Given a finite
\isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-trace \isa{{\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ c{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}acc{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}} of length \isa{m} ending in the canonical
accept config \isa{{\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}t{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharcomma}{\kern0pt}\ ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}accept{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}stage\ {\isacharparenleft}{\kern0pt}bl{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}{\isacharparenright}{\kern0pt}} and the walker
invariant at \isa{c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}} relative to a reachable \isa{cM}, deliver an
accepting \isa{M}-path from \isa{cM}.  Strong induction on \isa{m}; at
each level dispatch on the walker stage and peel one \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-step:

%
\begin{itemize}%
\item the five active stages (\isa{in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}read}, \isa{at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}compute},
\isa{in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write}, \isa{in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}advance}, \isa{at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}next}, and an active read
boundary) all have \isa{c{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}\ {\isasymnoteq}\ c{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}acc}, so \isa{m\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ Suc\ m{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}; peel
the step via the matching preservation lemma (\isa{at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}compute} emits
one \isa{M}-step into the \isa{in{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}write} witness; \isa{at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}next} emits
one via \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}cycle{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}close} and advances \isa{cM}), then
recurse on \isa{m{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}};

\item a boundary at the accept config closes the induction:
\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}simulates{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}accept{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}iff} forces \isa{mt{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}state\ cM\ {\isacharequal}{\kern0pt}\ t{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M};

\item a boundary at the reject config is impossible — the trace runs to
the accept config, but reject is terminal (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reject{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}terminal})
and the reject config is not the accept config.

The conclusion is in \isa{rtrancl} form for the downstream
\isa{Lang{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm}-repacking in \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}language}.%
\end{itemize}%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%

\begin{isamarkuptext}%
Classical language-equivalence (biconditional) for alphabet
  reduction: an \isa{{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}a}-word \isa{w} over the input alphabet is in
  \isa{M}'s language iff its \isa{sym{\isadigit{4}}}-encoding is in the language
  of the reduced machine \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}.  Pairs the forward inclusion
  \isa{alphabet{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reduce{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}language{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}forward} (in
  \isa{AlphabetReduction{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}Theorems{\isachardot}{\kern0pt}thy}) with the reverse leg supplied by
  \isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}simulation{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}phase{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}chunked{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}reverse}.

  Unlike AE, the alphabet-reduction construction has no input
  validation prefix (the no-validation design point), so the reverse
  direction needs neither a validation-peel nor a determinism /
  chain-uniqueness argument: the encoded input's accepting \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}}-run
  is handed to the engine directly off the initial read-boundary
  correspondence (\isa{ar{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}walker{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}at{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}boundary}, the conjunction of the
  three \isa{{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}init} invariants).  No \isa{det{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm} hypothesis is
  required.

  The \isa{set\ w\ {\isasymsubseteq}\ Sigma{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}tm\ M} guard is required (and matches
  AE's statement): \isa{Lang{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm} bakes in the input-alphabet
  restriction, so \isa{w\ {\isasymin}\ Lang{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm\ M} supplies the guard for
  free in the forward direction, but membership of the encoded word
  in \isa{Lang{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm\ M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}} says nothing about \isa{w}'s alphabet.  For
  \isa{w} outside the input alphabet the encoded word can still be
  accepted by \isa{M{\isacharprime}{\kern0pt}} while \isa{w\ {\isasymnotin}\ Lang{\isacharunderscore}{\kern0pt}mttm\ M}.%
\end{isamarkuptext}\isamarkuptrue%
